title: Launch Burn-and-Recovery Protocol and KPI Runway
content:
Purpose:
This working doc defines a compact burn-and-recovery protocol for feature launches that are latency- and cost-sensitive (hosted API + dedicated). Focus: detect early cost burn or latency degradation, enact staged mitigations, and restore to baseline within agreed SLA windows.

Goals:
- Keep 99.9th percentile latency within target for the first 72h post-launch.
- Contain incremental token cost increase to < 20% of baseline during pilot window.
- Recovery action timeline: detect (T0), triage (T0+15m), mitigation (T0+45m), recovery confirmation (T0+3h).

Quick summary of metrics (operational):
- Baseline RPS (per-route): 120 rps
- Expected pilot peak: 600 rps (5x) for first 2 hours
- Baseline cost/unit: $0.0025 per 1k tokens
- Alert thresholds: token spend growth > 25% over rolling 1h, 95p latency > 350ms, error rate > 0.5%

KPI runway (tracked values and owner formulas):
- Daily active routes (owner: Priya): current / target / delta
- Median latency by model (owner: Ethan): measured in ms, compare rolling 30m to baseline
- Cost burn rate (owner: Jordan): incremental cost per 1k requests = (observed_cost - baseline_cost) / baseline_requests
- Quality regressions (owner: Lena): % of prompts with flagged hallucination or missing intents from eval suite

Milestone tracker (simple status rows - update in sync calls):
- Milestone: Canary release (owner: Priya) — Target date: 2025-03-09 — Status: planned — Acceptance: 0.1% traffic, smoke tests green
- Milestone: 24h pilot (owner: Jordan) — Target date: 2025-03-11 — Status: scheduled — Acceptance: latency <= baseline+10% and cost burn < 20%
- Milestone: Scale to GA (owner: Product) — Target date: 2025-03-25 — Status: depends on pilot

Readiness checklist (pre-launch quick checks):
- [ ] Canary traffic route configured + fallback route (smoke validation URL)
- [ ] Canary SLOs and alerts created (95p latency, error rate, token spend)
- [ ] Ops rotation assigned for first 48h with escalation ladder
- [ ] Rollback playbook ready (model pin + traffic cutover play)
- [ ] Cost-guard rails applied (burst quota, rate limits)
- [ ] Eval prompt set uploaded and baseline scores recorded

Burn detection runbook (first 60 minutes):
1) Detect: automated alert fires (token burn or latency). Capture a 10m and 1h window snapshot.
2) Triage (owner: oncall): determine whether burn is traffic-driven, model-quality-driven, or infra (GPU throttling / queueing).
3) Immediate mitigations (choose the minimal effective action):
   - Short-term: reduce canary traffic to 5% or enable rate-limits at gateway.
   - Mid-term: switch canary to quantized model variant (same family) using traffic router.
   - Infrastructure: increase dedicated pool capacity (if on contract and autoscale slower than threshold).
4) Communication: post incident note in #launch-ops, update stakeholders (PM, Eng, SRE) with current action and ETA.

Recovery confirmation criteria:
- 95p latency within target for 30 consecutive minutes and token spend delta < 10% vs baseline.
- Quality regression rate <= pre-launch eval delta threshold (default: 1.2x).

Scenario playbooks (concise):
A) Traffic spike beyond forecast: enable burst quota, engage queue backpressure, throttle non-essential routes, expand dedicated pool if available. Owner: Infra oncall.
B) Model regression causing repeated retries (higher token spend): pin to prior model version, run quick eval against 50 recent canary prompts, run offline diff, escalate to Model Ops. Owner: Applied ML.
C) Region outage impacting latency: route to alternate region with fallback decoding configuration; enable regional read-only mode for non-critical features. Owner: SRE.

Cost calculation cheat sheet (quick):
- Example: baseline 100k tokens/h at $0.0025 per 1k tokens = $0.25/h baseline.
- If launch causes 40% token increase in pilot (140k tokens/h) => new cost = $0.35/h => incremental $0.10/h.
- Use batching improvements: aim for 20% token efficiency gain to offset half the burn.

Escalation ladder (contacts):
- Level 1: launch oncall (ops-channel) — Priya Nair — 15 min triage window
- Level 2: SRE lead — Ethan Zhao — 30 min decision window (scale / route change)
- Level 3: Product lead — Jordan Kim — 60 min decision (rollback / pause GA)

Open questions / notes to self: (fragmented for iteration)
- Need a lightweight endpoint to run eval prompts against live canary traffic without routing user traffic — action: ask infra for test-stub endpoint (JIRA-RI-3478).
- How granular should cost alerts be per-customer vs per-route? Current plan: per-route for first pilot, add per-customer in Phase 2.
- Investigate adding an automated rollback if cost delta persists > 2h despite mitigations.

Postmortem starter template (to be copied into Confluence after any incidence):
- Summary, timeline, root cause hypothesis, actions taken, recovery confirmation, follow-ups (owners + due dates), cost impact estimate, lessons learned.

Immediate next steps before canary:
- Priya: create canary routing + smoke test script (due 2025-03-02).
- Ethan: validate autoscale triggers against expected 5x spike (due 2025-03-04).
- Lena: finalize eval prompt set and baseline metrics export (due 2025-03-03).
- Jordan: draft comms template for launch-channel (done, attach to JIRA).

Appendix (short snippets and links):
- Smoke test checklist: health-check, token-count check, small-batch inference sanity, log sampling.
- Quick training: 15m walkthrough for ops rotation on how to flip traffic and pin model versions.
- Slack templates: incident open/update/close (copy on Confluence).

Notes on doc style: keep this compact — move step-by-step playbooks into separate single-responsibility files when stable. This should remain a lightweight single-pane runway that pairs KPI thresholds with concrete mitigations and owners.

(end of working draft)
